### Current evidence and source map

The checkout is pinned to 2fd89e1103a0ee1976e0e1a1210c2d4e1bb57de0. The registered public create-issue operation succeeded after direct helper invocation was hook-refused. Native Start created the #2146 actor/binding/timer normally. Missing last-known-state was normalized with native reconcile while detached and verified by GitHub readback. Direct bin/aitm.mjs draft-branch then completed with the same generation and timer start. These observations demonstrate a prevention sequence in this new checkout, not recovery of #2145.

scripts/task-tracker/draft-branch.mjs reads live board/ownership and location, then creates an undated journal and switches branches before ordinary Start renewal. It does not check the last-known-state marker before those effects. lib/native-branch-renewal.mjs enforces exact native carrier, original generation, clean physical source/index/ref/reflog, singleton owner, body/board state equality, and latest durable location equality. The final state and location checks explain why the supplied partial attempt cannot pass current renewal even after state normalization alone.

task-tracker.mjs calls enforceIssueWorktreeLocation before runVerbPreflight. lib/worktree-relocation-guard.mjs obtains the session with fallback-to-empty behavior, writes location through mutateIssueBody, and excludes reconcile from the guarded verb set. lib/issue-worktree-location.mjs validates structural history but location equality ignores SID. state.mjs loads actor timing, and lib/timing-actor.mjs rejects default-session. Together these source paths match the supplied terminal sequence: an unattributed named location can be appended before timing refuses. This is not yet a reproduced result in a disposable fixture.

verbs/reconcile.mjs accept-live stamps another visit, ignores the returned writeIssueBodyWithRetry outcome, then persists local state. Its stdout is insufficient evidence. #2146 used actual body/board readback; its second Backlog entry remains history.

Existing integration/native-branch-observation tests exercise physical Git but call the inspector directly with substituted remote reads. ### Current evidence and source map

The checkout is pinned to 2fd89e1103a0ee1976e0e1a1210c2d4e1bb57de0. The registered public create-issue operation succeeded after direct helper invocation was hook-refused. Native Start created the #2146 actor/binding/timer normally. Missing last-known-state was normalized with native reconcile while detached and verified by GitHub readback. Direct bin/aitm.mjs draft-branch then completed with the same generation and timer start. These observations demonstrate a prevention sequence in this new checkout, not recovery of #2145.

scripts/task-tracker/draft-branch.mjs reads live board/ownership and location, then creates an undated journal and switches branches before ordinary Start renewal. It does not check the last-known-state marker before those effects. lib/native-branch-renewal.mjs enforces exact native carrier, original generation, clean physical source/index/ref/reflog, singleton owner, body/board state equality, and latest durable location equality. The final state and location checks explain why the supplied partial attempt cannot pass current renewal even after state normalization alone.

task-tracker.mjs calls enforceIssueWorktreeLocation before runVerbPreflight. lib/worktree-relocation-guard.mjs obtains the session with fallback-to-empty behavior, writes location through mutateIssueBody, and excludes reconcile from the guarded verb set. lib/issue-worktree-location.mjs validates structural history but location equality ignores SID. state.mjs loads actor timing, and lib/timing-actor.mjs rejects default-session. Together these source paths match the supplied terminal sequence: an unattributed named location can be appended before timing refuses. This is not yet a reproduced result in a disposable fixture.

verbs/reconcile.mjs accept-live stamps another visit, ignores the returned writeIssueBodyWithRetry outcome, then persists local state. Its stdout is insufficient evidence. #2146 used actual body/board readback; its second Backlog entry remains history.

Existing integration/native-branch-observation tests exercise physical Git but call the inspector directly with substituted remote reads. The registered public create-issue operation succeeded after direct helper invocation was hook-refused. Native Start created the #2146 actor/binding/timer normally. These observations demonstrate a prevention sequence in this new checkout, not recovery of #2145.\n\nscripts/task-tracker/draft-branch.mjs reads live board/ownership and location, then creates an undated journal and switches branches before ordinary Start renewal. It does not check the last-known-state marker before those effects. lib/native-branch-renewal.mjs enforces exact native carrier, original generation, clean physical source/index/ref/reflog, singleton owner, body/board state equality, and latest durable location equality. The final state and location checks explain why the supplied partial attempt cannot pass current renewal even after state normalization alone.\n\ntask-tracker.mjs calls enforceIssueWorktreeLocation before runVerbPreflight. lib/worktree-relocation-guard.mjs obtains the session with fallback-to-empty behavior, writes location through mutateIssueBody, and excludes reconcile from the guarded verb set. lib/issue-worktree-location.mjs validates structural history but location equality ignores SID. state.mjs loads actor timing, and lib/timing-actor.mjs rejects default-session. Together these source paths match the supplied terminal sequence: an unattributed named location can be appended before timing refuses. This is not yet a reproduced result in a disposable fixture.\n\nverbs/reconcile.mjs accept-live stamps another visit, ignores the returned writeIssueBodyWithRetry outcome, then persists local state. Its stdout is insufficient evidence. #2146 used actual body/board readback; its second Backlog entry remains history.\n\nExisting integration/native-branch-observation tests exercise physical Git but call the inspector directly with substituted remote reads. Existing disposable-worktree-lifecycle tests replace renewBinding with setActiveTask. Neither establishes public-hook/public-CLI recovery of the preserved failure. Use the pinned production hook/public CLI and ordinary state/location/binding writers. Keep inherited genuine native identity for the positive fixture; isolate all provider data under .scratch and intercept only provider transport. The test harness must refuse any unhandled provider request and any remote Git write. Do not copy live runtime. Preserve fixture roots and all unsuccessful logs. If the necessary harness cannot satisfy these boundaries, report that blocker instead of using a weaker proof.\n\nOnly after both baseline reproductions, experiment with one small throwaway candidate at a time. Candidate A checks actor and applicable semantic authority before location mutation and again under the issue lock. Candidate B admits only a digest-bound initial-branch recovery manifest that binds original generation/timer, physical ref/reflog, journal and both exact historical locations, preserving them with an append-only correction. Candidate C validates missing state before journal/checkout and reads normalization back. The final report will state which candidate classes were actually exercised.\n\nRequired matrix: missing/wrong actor; malformed or conflicting state; journal mismatch; owner/generation/timer drift; dirty tracked, staged, untracked, source/ref/reflog drift; remote owner/state/location drift at lock/write; provider write and readback failure; history preservation; no-push. For every required case record pass, refusal, not run or blocked, with its scope and commands. Do not turn a not-run case into a pass.\n\nActivation is an independent feasibility condition. Trace the installed/scoped-versus-repo-relative hook and public-entry selection. Establish whether reviewed support can become the actually selected runtime of the preserved blocked checkout without source-byte drift, manual installation, copied state, live merge/rebase/push or an alternate command evading the old hook. Publish findings and the proposed defect plan through #2146's governed comment/artifact operations. The report verifier must check artifact inventory, source identities and explicit matrix coverage without treating missing runs as passing. No source commits are intended; never attribute the pinned HEAD to #2146 as a commit trail.\n\n### Risks and limits\n\nNo #2145 local runtime has been read by this chat; exact local historical facts come from its owning handoff. Adaptive plan-estimate refused `estimation-runtime:rubric-issue-unconfigured`; checked-in configuration is rubric 0. The registered supplied-hours compatibility command wrote the prospective estimate, without a fabricated forecast or configuration change. Plan approval applied only to this authorized spike.\n\nThese admission findings are collateral observations; they have not been expanded into production fixes or separate defect issues.\n\n## Disposable reproduction attempt\n\nCommands executed from the owned source checkout:\n\n```sh\nnode .scratch/native-recovery-spike/run-baseline.mjs setup\nnode .scratch/native-recovery-spike/run-baseline.mjs start\n```\n\nSetup exited 0. Source `runtime-storage.mjs:37-53` intentionally checks all enclosing Git roots and rejects artifact-owned runtime; lines 172-184 apply this before alias/foreign-root handling. `scripts/tests/helpers/runtime-root-fixture.mjs` uses `.ai-task-manager/runtime/test-fixtures`, which is outside this spike's authorized experiment bucket. No such fixture was created here.\n\n## Harness limits\n\nOnly provider transport was intended to be substituted. The preload also propagates itself to Node descendants to keep provider calls contained; it does not replace guards, binding, timing, ownership, locks, Git results or runtime admission. It rejects unknown provider requests and remote Git commands. However, no provider request was reached, so its behavior is **unqualified**. Empty current hook outputs contain no block, but the original runner checked status alone; the reviewer identified status-zero JSON refusals. The runner now parses block/deny decisions, without rerunning the blocked baseline. This remains instrumented direct-process evidence, not proof of host hook selection or package activation. No candidate source prototype was created or run.\n\nThe artifact manifest is a post-run inventory, not a retrospective execution receipt; instrumentation hashes were not captured at execution. A later readback-plus-redirection command for #2145 was hook-refused as WRITE_OTHER before execution, so it supplied no new issue snapshot. That write was not retried through another transport.\n\n## Source-to-experiment map\n\n| Question | Owning source at the pin | Evidence and limit |\n|---|---|---|\n| Fixture admission | `lib/runtime-storage.mjs:37-53,172-184`; `lib/action-capture.mjs:200`; `bin/aitm.mjs:99-108` | Observed public CLI refusal before bind, exit 1; no admission bypass. |\n| A: actor/semantic checks before location | `task-tracker.mjs:507-568`; `lib/worktree-relocation-guard.mjs:107-192`; `state.mjs`; `lib/timing-actor.mjs:11-28` | Source orders location before preflight actor-timing load. Preservation properties require integration proof. |\n| C: state normalization | `draft-branch.mjs:112-169`; `lib/native-branch-renewal.mjs:276-291`; `verbs/reconcile.mjs:402-464` | No pre-check of body state before journal/checkout.       "body": "# Native branch prevention and bounded recovery implementation plan\n\n> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:executing-plans for authorized native implementation, or superpowers:subagent-driven-development if the owner selects that approach. This proposal is NOT authorization to implement. Its qualification and activation gates remain unsatisfied.\n\n**Goal:** Prevent location mutation by an invalid actor and partial draft checkout caused by missing state; qualify a narrowly attributable recovery of an already-partial initial branch only when runtime activation is demonstrably available.\n\n**Architecture:** Validate actor and applicable semantic authority before every location effect, and revalidate under the existing issue lock and fresh-body writer. Separate verified state normalization from branch creation. Preserve legacy journals and history; a new explicit recovery operation may consume a digest-bound observation and reuse ordinary binding writers, but may never broaden ordinary Start or silently discard the fallback-actor location.\n\n**Tech stack:** Node.js ESM, existing AITM public command registry and lifecycle guards, real Git worktrees, GitHub transport seams, `node:test`.\n\n**Spec:** #2146 Scope and mirrored investigation plan, https://github.com/kburson/ai-task-manager/issues/2146#issuecomment-6610204792; findings in `report.md`. Source baseline `2fd89e1103a0ee1976e0e1a1210c2d4e1bb57de0`.\n\n## Global constraints\n\n- Production implementation requires owner review and explicit authorization after this spike.\n- No #2145 live repair, foreign-root access, identity override, transcript-guessing identity, copied runtime, skipped timing, generic foreign-worktree allowance or weakened ordinary Start.\n- Preserve both historical location markers verbatim. Do not append a fictitious HEAD location while the physical branch is named.\n- The original legacy journal has no generation or time. Never retrofit those fields as historical evidence.\n- Preserve original active timer, boundAt, wordsAtStart and occupancy generation; preserve Unknown timing rather than manufacturing a duration.\n- No live rebase/merge/push/reset/ref deletion/cleanup, old-worktree changes, #2071 bridge proof or protected issue closure within qualification.\n- Physical integration tests must run production hook decisions, public CLI, ordinary writers and real Git. Only provider transport is substitutable.\n\n## Review focus\n\n1. A hook may emit JSON block with status zero: the harness must refuse dispatch on either policy block or nonzero exit.\n2. Local issue locks cannot lease remote ownership/state: re-read before effects and fresh-body retries; ambiguity or post-write drift must remain an explicit partial result.\n3. A legacy journal cannot identify a generation: require independent current actor/occupancy/timer observations and explicit legacy provenance; refuse inconsistent evidence.\n4. Successful stdout is not a committed remote write: only verified write/readback may admit cache, journal, checkout or bind effects.\n5. Candidate code selected in a disposable fixture says nothing about old-hook activation in #2145: qualification and delivery must retain separate evidence.\n\n## Prerequisite gate 0 — qualify the experiment and activation contract\n\nThis is a decision gate, not permission to change runtime admission. The current `.scratch` fixture failed before bind with `ROOT_OVERRIDE_UNSAFE`. Its provider double has never received a request.\n\nThe proposed qualification location is the existing repository convention `.ai-task-manager/runtime/test-fixtures/2146-native-recovery-*`; evidence can remain under `.scratch/native-recovery-spike`. The owner must authorize this scope change before a follow-up experiment. Do not edit `runtime-storage.mjs`, use its test adapters, add aliases, or relocate existing evidence to evade the refusal.\n\nThe original runtime activation contract is also unresolved. The old hook admits only strict Start renewal; bootstrap refuses an already-bound session. There is no established old-hook-admitted operation to install/select reviewed support under the stated frozen-source rules. Identify such a supported operation or obtain a separately reviewed change to that constraint. Until then, Tasks 1–2 can be reviewed as future prevention work, while recovery activation and Task 3 live use remain held. A future release in a fresh checkout is not recovery of the old attempt.\n\n## Task 1 — actor and semantic authority before location mutation\n\n**Files:** modify `scripts/task-tracker/task-tracker.mjs`, `scripts/task-tracker/lib/worktree-relocation-guard.mjs`, `scripts/task-tracker/lib/verb-preflight.mjs`; create `scripts/task-tracker/lib/location-mutation-authority.mjs` and `scripts/tests/integration/task-tracker/location-mutation-authority.test.mjs`. Reuse `issue-mutator-lock.mjs`, `ownership-policy.mjs` and `timing-actor.mjs` without weakening their predicates.\n\n**Interfaces:**\n\n```ts\ntype LocationAuthority = {\n  issueNumber: number; root: string; verb: string;\n  actor: { provider: string; sid: string; timingActorKey: string; viewer: string };\n  bindingDigest: string | null; occupancyDigest: string | null;\n  bodyVersion: number; bodyDigest: string; boardState: string; owners: string[];\n};\nreadLocationMutationAuthority(ctx): Promise<LocationAuthority>;\nassertLocationMutationAuthority(ctx, expected: LocationAuthority): Promise<void>;\n```\n\n`ctx` is the existing public tracker context from `runtime.mjs::buildContext`; no caller-supplied actor override is added. `readLocationMutationAuthority` resolves the provider's actual session, validates its timing key, and runs applicable existing ownership/state/bind predicates without writes. First bind may have null binding/occupancy digests, but still requires a genuine provider actor and the normal target authority. Confirmation authorizes a location change only; it does not waive actor or semantic checks.\n\n- Write failing public-CLI tests: native initial Start succeeds; terminal with no provider SID and `--confirm-relocation` refuses with body, timing, occupancy and local binding unchanged; wrong/multiple owner, closed issue, wrong target and semantic state refusal likewise write nothing.\n- Run `node --test scripts/tests/integration/task-tracker/location-mutation-authority.test.mjs` against the pin and retain the target failure. Do not accept a fixture-admission failure as this red test.\n- Move/factor read-only preflight before location mutation. Acquire the existing issue lock as the actual owner, re-read actor/binding/remote authority, and require `assertLocationMutationAuthority` from `mutateIssueBody`'s fresh-base validation on every retry. Preserve later ordinary verb checks; do not bulk move all preflight code without auditing its write behavior.\n- Add race tests where owner, board, location, actor state or generation changes after initial inspection and again at fresh-base write. Require refusal before the location write. If remote mutation races after the last observation, return a recorded partial/indeterminate outcome rather than claiming a cross-resource transaction.\n- Run the focused tests green and the existing relocation/preflight/ownership suites affected by these files; obtain review and commit under the subsequently authorized defect issue.\n\n## Task 2 — verified state readiness before draft journal and checkout\n\n**Files:** modify `scripts/task-tracker/draft-branch.mjs`, `scripts/task-tracker/verbs/reconcile.mjs`; create `scripts/task-tracker/lib/initial-branch-state.mjs` and `scripts/tests/integration/task-tracker/initial-branch-state.test.mjs`. Inspect and retain `writeIssueBodyWithRetry`'s actual return contract before editing its caller.\n\n**Interfaces:**\n\n```ts\ntype InitialBranchState = { issueNumber: number; state: string; bodyVersion: number; bodyDigest: string };\nreadInitialBranchState({ issueNumber, cfg }): Promise<InitialBranchState>;\nassertInitialBranchStateUnchanged(expected: InitialBranchState, cfg): Promise<void>;\n```\n\nMissing, duplicate/malformed or conflicting last-known-state yields a typed refusal before any journal/ref/checkout effect. For a clean detached initial attempt, the diagnostic recommends the existing ordinary `reconcile accept-live` route. `draft-branch` does not normalize state implicitly.\n\n- Reproduce the original missing-state failure through public draft-branch and its real ordinary Start child, after successful ordinary fixture bind. Assert the baseline leaves physical named branch plus legacy local HEAD and journal. Keep that failed fixture.\n- Add prevention tests expecting no journal/ref/checkout mutation for missing, malformed or conflicting state. Add the positive ordinary reconcile → verified readback → direct draft sequence, asserting unchanged generation and timer across renewal.\n- In reconcile, inspect write status and verified returned body/readback before `persistTrackerState`, audit-success or success return. On refused, ambiguous or mismatched readback, preserve prior local state and return a typed incomplete result. Do not hand-stamp fields or silently erase the extra entry visit generated by the existing reconciler.\n- In draft-branch, validate before journal creation and revalidate state/owner under the mutation lock immediately before checkout. A later remote drift still produces an explicit partial attempt with retained evidence, never an automatic rollback or broad renewal exception.\n- Test failed write, successful response with stale readback, matching marker with wrong board, drift at checkout, and normal verified success. Run `node --test scripts/tests/integration/task-tracker/initial-branch-state.test.mjs`, then relevant existing draft/reconcile suites. Review and commit separately from Task 1.\n\n## Task 3 — conditional exact initial-attempt recovery\n\n**Files:** create `scripts/task-tracker/lib/initial-branch-recovery.mjs`, `scripts/task-tracker/verbs/recover-initial-branch.mjs`, and `scripts/tests/integration/task-tracker/initial-branch-recovery.test.mjs`; modify `bin/aitm-registry.mjs`, public tracker dispatch, native command admission in `bash-guard.mjs`/`activity-guard.mjs`, `lib/issue-worktree-location.mjs`, and `draft-branch.mjs` for future journal versioning. Update command-surface guidance/self-doc through existing generation and validation, never manual drifted installed files.\n\n**Interfaces and artifact:**\n\n```ts\ntype RecoveryManifest = {\n  schema: 'aitm.initial-branch-recovery/v1';\n  repository: string; issueNumber: number; root: string; sid: string;\n  sourceCommit: string; oldBranch: 'HEAD'; physicalBranch: string;\n  journal: { digest: string; schema: 'legacy' | 'v2'; generationRecorded: string | null };\n  activeDigest: string; occupancyDigest: string; timingDigest: string;\n  bindingGenerationId: string; entryStartTs: string; boundAt: string; wordsAtStart: number;\n  refDigest: string; reflogDigest: string;\n  bodyVersion: number; bodyDigest: string; exactLocationMarkers: string[];\n  owners: string[]; boardState: string; recordedState: string | null;\n  provenance: 'current-observation';\n};\ninspectInitialBranchRecovery(ctx): Promise<{ manifest: RecoveryManifest; digest: string }>;\napplyInitialBranchRecovery(ctx, manifest: RecoveryManifest, expectedDigest: string):\n  Promise<{ status: 'recovered' | 'refused' | 'partial'; reason?: string }>;\n```\n\nThe manifest is a new current observation, never proof that the old journal contained generation/time. Future v2 journals record genuine generation, timer reference and creation time at creation; the existing legacy journal is preserved byte-for-byte. For legacy recovery, require matching original actor, active record, occupancy, timing, journal issue/root/head/branch, clean physical source, exact checkout reflog, open singleton owner and exact two-location history. A legacy journal alone never suffices. Reject any ambiguity in connecting the current preserved state to the historical attempt; timestamps alone establish no authority.\n\n- Write red tests using the two baseline failures in sequence: ordinary native bind; failed draft; ordinary missing-native-session terminal Start that appends the named `default-session` location then fails timing. Assert both marker bytes are retained before testing the candidate.\n- Expose closed future public forms `recover-initial-branch N --inspect` and `recover-initial-branch N --apply <manifest-path> --digest <sha256>`. Both require the genuine owning native actor and exact selected runtime. The hook observation is read-only; the CLI repeats all predicates under the issue lock. This is proposed new support, **not a command the old #2145 hook currently admits**.\n- Normalize missing state only through the verified Task 2 writer with fresh readback. Append an attributable correction/supersession record referencing digests of the exact two historical markers and manifest. Preserve history literally; do not ignore all fallback-actor records or rewrite the current physical branch as HEAD.\n- After fresh readback, renew through the existing ordinary Start/resume binding writer in-process using an internal, non-exported one-use recovery authorization. Do not write active-task/occupancy/timing records directly. The capability is bound to the observed generation, journal/body digests and physical checkout, and cannot be enabled through environment variables or broad flags. Ordinary Start keeps its current strict path.\n- Inject failure between every effect. A retry must recognize only its exact verified append-only record and unchanged generation/timer. Uncertain completion returns partial, retains evidence, and never overwrites history or resets the branch.\n- Run `node --test scripts/tests/integration/task-tracker/initial-branch-recovery.test.mjs` only after the two baseline reproductions. Required refusals: missing/wrong actor; journal mismatch; owner/generation/timer drift; dirty tracked/index/untracked/source/ref/reflog; conflicting state or extra location; stale manifest; remote drift at lock/write; write failure/readback mismatch; capability reuse/foreign target. Positive assertions include unchanged original timer/generation, both markers verbatim, exactly one correction, idempotent retry and zero push.\n\n## Activation and recovery sequence — still held\n\n1. Obtain owner authorization for the supported fixture location and complete both baseline reproductions with a qualified transport/hook runner.\n2. Review Tasks 1–3 and authorize only the desired production slices. Use native tracked defect issues; none were created by this spike.\n3. Qualify the future runtime in a separate clean supported fixture, including source/installed entry/hook selection digests and the complete refusal matrix. Preserve failed attempts.\n4. Establish a reviewed activation operation **admitted by the old hook** for the original checkout, or explicitly revise the activation constraints through owner review. There is no executable step 4 under the current constraints. Do not substitute bootstrap, manual installation, an alternate process or source edits and call it recovery.\n5. Only after step 4 is proven and the owner authorizes live recovery, have the original owner collect fresh local and GitHub evidence. Re-check the supplied historical hashes; a mismatch stops, rather than resetting state to those hashes.\n6. Apply exactly the reviewed digest-bound operation, read back its append-only audit and ordinary bind result, verify timer/generation/history/no-push, and report recovery separately from delivery, closure or the #2071 proof.\n\n## Self-review and limits\n\nQuestions A/C map to Tasks 1/2; B maps to Task 3; D is the explicit activation hold; E maps to gate 0 and every public integration test. All five review-focus cases have owning test steps. Function/type names agree across tasks. Tests must be failing for the intended product defect, not fixture admission. No proposed interface has been implemented or experimentally proven here. Owner review is required before production work; retaining the hold is the supported outcome if activation remains unavailable.\n\n<!-- aitm-owned-comment key=\"spike.defect-plan-v1\" -->",

      "body": "# Independent read-only review — #2146\n\nReviewer: `/root/activation_review`. Reviewed pinned source and preserved harness logs; no tests, mutations, foreign-root access or live recovery performed.\n\n## Findings accepted by the author\n\n1. No supported activation route was found under the frozen original-root constraints. Hooks choose the cwd scoped package then repo source; the selected CLI delegates relative to its own module. Renewal checks the selected public entry and unchanged physical source. Bootstrap refuses a bound session. Reviewing a different checkout changes none of these selections.\n2. Missing last-known-state and latest named location versus local HEAD are independent strict-renewal refusals. State normalization alone cannot recover the supplied attempt.\n3. The legacy draft journal lacks generation and time. It cannot independently attest either. Existing ordinary same-active Start and occupancy code appear to preserve them, but this remains source-only.\n4. `resolveRuntimeRoot` checks every enclosing repository and rejects the fixture under the owning root's `.scratch`. No existing public exception was found. Runtime adapter substitution would violate the provider-only experiment contract.\n5. The baseline stopped before bind, not at either target failure. All recovery candidates are unrun.\n6. The harness originally checked hook process status only, although bash-guard can emit a JSON policy block at status zero. The preserved attempt's outputs are empty, so no policy block is shown. The author subsequently added JSON block/deny detection; this correction has not been exercised by another baseline run and does not qualify the harness.\n7. The preload instruments child-process/network transport and propagates `--import` to Node descendants. The result is direct-process instrumentation, not native-host activation proof. There were zero provider requests, so the provider double's response/write behavior is unqualified. Source tree equality covers tracked bytes, not dependencies or whole-runtime provenance.\n\n## Disposition\n\nAll findings are accepted. Report fixture admission as observed; report recovery and activation as blocked/unproven. Preserve fixture and logs. Do not substitute runtime admission, move the fixture outside the authorized bucket, or treat old helper tests as public recovery evidence. The proposed plan must require a separately authorized fixture location and an independently established activation path before claiming recoverability.\n\n## Final artifact review\n\nThe reviewer found two P2 reporting inaccuracies: ordinary shared dependency symlinks do not enforce read-only access, and the provider instrumentation logs each Git delegation twice. The author corrected the report to disclose writable dependency links and absent dependency-byte inventory, and to identify 18 ledger entries as nine invocations. The old identity record is retained verbatim with its overstated label explicitly corrected in the report. The runner's future identity label was corrected without rerunning a baseline. No additional plan, blocked-status or activation-boundary finding was raised.\n\n<!-- aitm-owned-comment key=\"spike.read-only-review-v1\" -->",

      "body": "# #2146 native recovery follow-up — tested findings\n\nThe two target failures are reproduced through the pinned public CLI and ordinary binding writers in new physical repositories at the authorized fixture location. Small disposable prevention and normalization prototypes pass their bounded cases. **Exact recovery of the preserved #2145 attempt and activation of new support in its frozen old runtime remain blocked.** No production source was changed and no live recovery was attempted.\n\n## Authority and identities\n\nThe owner authorized this follow-up at 2026-11-03T23:29:25.183Z. Native #2146 resume began at 23:30:57.527Z, with experiments capped at 2026-11-04T01:10:57Z and handoff at 01:30:57Z. Native active duration remains Unknown; wall time is not substituted for it. The old v1 artifacts and refused `.scratch` fixture are retained unchanged.\n\nOwned source: `2fd89e1103a0ee1976e0e1a1210c2d4e1bb57de0`, branch `codex/2146-draft`. New physical repositories are under `.ai-task-manager/runtime/test-fixtures/2146-native-recovery-*`. Evidence is in `.scratch/native-recovery-spike/followup-20261103T233057Z/`. Every setup records source tree, independent fixture commit/tree, deliberate candidate patches and genuine current native SID. Fixture issue #2146 is a local provider record, not a copy of live runtime.\n\nBefore each public execution the harness freezes its own bytes and provider preload, records selected CLI/guard realpaths and hashes, source tree/status, dependency inventory digest, provider snapshot and actual identity environment. Later runs also freeze the exact GraphQL query catalogue, hook-config hash and complete `.tmp` contents before/after. Shared dependency symlinks are ordinary writable links; hashes are checked before/after, not described as filesystem-enforced read-only. Candidate code is committed only within its independent disposable repository before binding.\n\nThe CLI and both production guards are selected from each fixture's repository source; no scoped installed package exists. Production guards are directly invoked with constructed hook input, followed by the public CLI only after admission. Node children inherit the identified provider preload. **This is instrumented public-entry testing, not proof that the Codex native host selected or activated a new runtime.**\n\n## Transport qualification and preserved harness failures\n\n`baseline02` first Start at 23:35 exited zero without binding. Its preload omitted the native promisified `execFile` promise's `.child` property, so the ordinary stdin body writer never completed. That attempt remains unsuccessful evidence. Correcting the transport contract allowed public Start to create the binding normally.\n\nIndependent review identified shell containment, provider-shape and denial-parser gaps. Later harness versions refuse shell transport, validate repository arguments, reject unknown GraphQL queries through a frozen exact catalogue, supply requested repository/comment identity fields, and treat top-level block/deny, nested permission denial, nonzero exit, malformed JSON and unknown schemas as refusals. Unknown traffic is never delegated to real `gh`.\n\n`transport-qualification02.json` and its pre-execution receipt record successful reads and expected refusals for foreign repository/issue, unknown endpoint/query, direct fetch, shell subprocess and Git push. `qualification03` repeats these checks for the final transport version. The push probe was deliberately rejected before delegation: do not describe the entire experiment as having zero attempted push calls. Ordinary public Start proved real provider read/write/readback transport and binding creation. All fixture Git operations that were dispatched were local; no remote push was dispatched.\n\nThe fake provider is deliberately bounded, not a complete GitHub emulator or an OS network sandbox. It does not establish arbitrary GraphQL, pagination, installer subprocess or production network behavior. The early `baseline02` Start queued timing instead of posting it; its snapshots did not include the queue. Later qualified baselines include actual timing comments and complete `.tmp` evidence. Do not use v1/early evidence to claim complete timing-history preservation.\n\n## Observed product behavior\n\n| Case | Result and interpretation | Evidence |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| Missing-state baseline | Public Start succeeds detached.       "body": "# #2146 proposed native recovery defects — revised after follow-up experiments\n\nThis is a reviewable implementation proposal, **NOT authorization to implement** production fixes or recover #2145. Source baseline: `2fd89e1103a0ee1976e0e1a1210c2d4e1bb57de0`. Evidence: `report-v2.md`, exact run snapshots, and `matrix-v2.json`. The authorized spike created only disposable prototypes.\n\nUse the existing task workflow and execution/review skills when separately authorized. Create governed defect issues before production edits; do not invent issue numbers here. Specification/plan filenames for those issues must contain their eventual numeric IDs.\n\n## What the experiments changed\n\nBoth original failure shapes now reproduce through public CLI/ordinary writers at the authorized fixture location. The earlier root-admission blocker is resolved for experiments without changing runtime-storage. Moving existing preflight before location mutation and checking state before journal/checkout demonstrate viable prevention directions. Ordinary reconcile-before-draft succeeds with unchanged timer/generation.\n\nTwo further requirements are now experimentally grounded: current reconcile falsely claims success after rejected/dropped writes, and a one-time early remote snapshot cannot protect a later checkout. The revised disposable checks catch the tested cases. They are incomplete prototypes, not code ready to copy into production.\n\nThe old guard admits ordinary renewal for a clean normalized partial attempt, but still refuses an otherwise normalized attempt after the fallback location append. A detach-and-return with an equivalent final checkout is accepted: the current guard does not attest an exact full reflog history. Exact recovery therefore needs a separate observed-manifest contract; do not broaden ordinary Start to ignore history.\n\n## Invariants and boundaries\n\n- Preserve both historical location markers verbatim; append a truthful correction, never a fictitious HEAD marker or a blanket exemption for fallback SIDs.\n- The old journal lacks generation/time. `generationRecorded: null` is truthful; adding fields now cannot make them historical evidence.\n- Preserve the original active timer, boundAt, word baseline, occupancy owner and generation. Unknown timing remains Unknown.\n- Never fabricate active-task, occupancy, timing, evidence markers or a commit trail. Recovery must reuse ordinary writers with a narrowly checked in-process capability.\n- No frozen original checkout mutation, live recovery, package installation, source drift, identity/root override, generic foreign-worktree exception, rebase/merge/reset/ref deletion/push or #2071 bridge work is authorized here.\n- Local locks cannot lease GitHub state. Revalidate near effects and report partial completion honestly when a remote effect landed but later evidence is uncertain.\n- The separate no-code spike deliverable-marker defect is not part of these defects.\n\n## Independently useful delivery slices\n\nKeep sibling work packages with explicit dependencies and small reviewed stories. Estimates below are planning bounds, not accepted native estimates.\n\n| Slice | Suggested stories | Dependency / review boundary |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| A. Actor-safe location writes | A1 read-only authority interface and refusal tests, 2–4h; A2 integrate before entry and inside fresh writer, 2–4h | Useful independently; no recovery exception. |\n| B. Verified normalization and initial branch readiness | B1 reconcile outcome/readback contract, 2–4h; B2 readiness before journal/checkout and drift evidence, 3–4h | B2 consumes B1's verification result; retain ordinary normalization command. |\n| C. Exact recovery inspection | C1 immutable manifest and legacy provenance refusals, 3–4h | After A/B contracts; inspection does not imply activation or apply authority. |\n| D. Conditional recovery application | D1 append-only correction and ordinary writer adapter, 3–4h; D2 effect-boundary retry/refusal qualification, 3–4h | Held on activation decision and explicit production scope. Split further if any story exceeds 4h; hard cap 6h. |\n| E. Activation contract | Separate bounded design/qualification story, 2–4h initially | Not solved by adding a verb in a package the old host cannot load. Requires owner decision below. |\n\nEach slice needs its own reviewed/tested increment and native issue lifecycle. Independently review and integrate accepted increments without waiting for held recovery work; none of this waives repository or cross-provider review requirements.\n\n## Task 1 — actor and semantic authority before location effects\n\n**Owned files:** new `scripts/task-tracker/lib/location-mutation-authority.mjs`; integrate `scripts/task-tracker/task-tracker.mjs`, `lib/worktree-relocation-guard.mjs`, and existing actor/assignment readers. Tests: new `scripts/tests/integration/task-tracker/location-mutation-authority.test.mjs`, plus relevant relocation and preflight tests.\n\n```ts\ntype LocationAuthority = {\n  issue: number; repository: string; actor: { provider: string; sid: string };\n  worktree: string; branch: string; ownerDigest: string; state: string;\n  bodyVersion: number; bodyDigest: string;\n};\nreadLocationMutationAuthority(context): Promise<LocationAuthority>;\nassertLocationMutationAuthority(expected, fresh): void;\n```\n\nExtract a genuinely read-only preflight rather than copying the spike's move of the entire existing preflight. Reject invalid actor and applicable semantic authority before any location write. Bind authority to the genuine native actor and physical root; a syntactically valid timing key is correlation, not authorization. Preserve compatible non-native actor routes according to their existing supported identity contracts.\n\nAt the issue lock/fresh-body mutation closure, re-read actor, target, ownership/state and body authority. A body-version change must trigger revalidation, not reuse a stale preflight token. Keep normal bind/relocation semantics and side-effect ownership explicit. Do not move an unrelated lifecycle mutation earlier just to get validation.\n\n**Failing-first cases:** missing native actor/terminal fallback; malformed/default/unknown identity; genuine foreign actor in a supported independently owned test session (never forged env); wrong/multiple owner; ownership/state/body change between entry and writer; failed provider read; matching location with invalid actor; valid bind and confirmed relocation. Assert provider writes, binding and timing effects individually, not stdout alone. The spike proves missing actor and foreign-owner cases; other cases remain obligations.\n\n## Task 2 — verified normalization and branch readiness\n\n**Owned files:** `scripts/task-tracker/verbs/reconcile.mjs`, `lib/state-recording.mjs`, new `lib/initial-branch-state.mjs`, `scripts/task-tracker/draft-branch.mjs`; integration tests `scripts/tests/integration/task-tracker/initial-branch-state.test.mjs` plus existing draft/reconcile suites.\n\n```ts\ntype InitialBranchState = {\n  issue: number; ownerDigest: string; liveState: string; recordedState: string;\n  bodyVersion: number; bodyDigest: string;\n};\ninspectInitialBranchState(context): Promise<InitialBranchState>;\nassertInitialBranchReady(expected, fresh): void;\n```\n\nReconcile must consume the actual returned write outcome, then verified authoritative body/state readback before local persistence, success audit or success return. Refused/ambiguous writes return typed failure. If a write landed but fresh readback fails, return typed **partial** with retained evidence; do not claim nothing changed. Preserve existing diagnostic failure comments and visit history.\n\nPrefer a fresh-body transformation over the current snapshot writer where feasible; preserve concurrent unrelated content and explicitly refuse conflicting state/history. Review changes to the shared retry helper separately because callers may intentionally need soft failure after an already-committed board move.\n\nDraft-branch must check OPEN/singleton owner/local/live/recorded state before journal/ref/checkout, and revalidate under the existing issue-lock sequence as close as possible to the effect. Keep missing-state normalization explicit through ordinary reconcile while detached. Never normalize silently inside branch creation. Ensure authority reads are not accidentally placed outside a lock wait and then reused unchanged.\n\n**Failing-first cases:** missing/malformed/conflicting markers; successful reconcile→readback→draft; rejected writes; acknowledged but dropped writes/stale readback; fresh readback mismatch after a successful remote write; remote owner/state changes before lock, after snapshot, before checkout and before renewal; changed local binding/occupancy while waiting; clean no-journal refusal; retained partial-attempt evidence on later drift. Assert unchanged original generation/timer on success. A second read catches one tested race; it does not make GitHub and Git atomic.\n\n## Task 3 — conditional exact-attempt recovery\n\n**Owned files:** new `lib/initial-branch-recovery.mjs`, `verbs/recover-initial-branch.mjs`, `scripts/tests/integration/task-tracker/initial-branch-recovery.test.mjs`; public registry/dispatch; narrowly scoped command admission in bash/activity guards; `lib/issue-worktree-location.mjs`; future journal schema in `draft-branch.mjs`. Regenerate command guidance/self-doc through existing tooling.\n\n```ts\ntype RecoveryManifest = {\n  schema: 'aitm.initial-branch-recovery/v1';\n  repository: string; issueNumber: number; root: string; sid: string;\n  sourceCommit: string; selectedRuntimeDigest: string;\n  oldBranch: 'HEAD'; physicalBranch: string;\n  journal: { digest: string; schema: 'legacy' | 'v2'; generationRecorded: string | null };\n  activeDigest: string; occupancyDigest: string; timingDigest: string;\n  bindingGenerationId: string; entryStartTs: string; boundAt: string; wordsAtStart: number;\n  refDigest: string; reflogDigest: string; bodyVersion: number; bodyDigest: string;\n  exactLocationMarkers: string[]; owners: string[];\n  boardState: string; recordedState: string | null; provenance: 'current-observation';\n};\ninspectInitialBranchRecovery(context): Promise<{ manifest: RecoveryManifest; digest: string }>;\napplyInitialBranchRecovery(context, manifest, expectedDigest):\n  Promise<{ status: 'recovered' | 'refused' | 'partial'; reason?: string }>;\n```\n\nThe manifest is an observation made now, not a retrospective receipt. A legacy journal alone cannot prove original generation/timer. Require independent actor, active-record, occupancy, timing and supplied historical evidence; refuse ambiguity. Pin full relevant refs/reflog observations, not merely the last checkout message. Future v2 journals may record generation and time at creation; never retrofit old journals.\n\nProposed closed commands are `recover-initial-branch N --inspect` and `recover-initial-branch N --apply <manifest-path> --digest <sha256>`. These commands **do not exist in the pinned runtime**. Both require the genuine owning native actor and exact selected runtime. Hooks inspect read-only; CLI repeats predicates under the lock. No env-activated capability or broad override.\n\nAfter independently verified Task 2 normalization, append a correction/supersession record referencing the manifest and both exact historical marker digests. Preserve both historical location markers verbatim. Use a private one-use in-process capability for the existing Start/resume binding writer, scoped to issue/root/generation/journal/body/checkout. Never directly rewrite active-task, occupancy or timing. Ordinary Start keeps its strict path.\n\nInject failure between every effect. Retry recognizes only its own verified correction and unchanged generation/timer. A post-write ambiguity is partial, not a reason to roll back refs or erase history. An exact manifest must detect intervening equivalent detach/return history that ordinary renewal currently accepts.\n\n**Still unexecuted:** exact recovery positive; wrong actor/journal/generation/timer; malformed state and extra history; source/index/untracked/ref/full-reflog drift against a manifest; stale digest; owner/state drift at every lock/write boundary; write/readback failures for correction; capability reuse/foreign target; crash retry/idempotence. Preserve original timer/generation, exactly one attributable correction, both markers and no delegated push. Existing ordinary-renewal evidence does not count as these recovery tests.\n\n## Activation contract and required owner decision\n\nActual old-runtime probes are recorded in the report. Exact Start is refused by state authority, and remains refused by durable location even in the separately normalized fallback-location fixture. Registered/public installer, installer CLI, self-link, doctor and reconcile are denied for binding mismatch. The setup script reaches an earlier absent-projection refusal in the fixture; it is not proof of a supported route. Native-host activation was not demonstrated.\n\nThe registered installer runs from already-selected package source. It neither acquires a new reviewed runtime nor makes an unrecognized new command admissible to an old frozen hook. Adding a package-selection manifest to future code alone cannot make an old loader read it. There is **no executable activation step under all current constraints**.\n\nThe minimum future activation design needs: immutable reviewed package/source digest; explicit old-loader or trusted-host admission; exact owning actor/root/generation binding; atomic selection with recoverable failure; actual hook and public-CLI selected-path/hash readback; original source/runtime preservation. Before approval, show the concrete supported command and its host authorization model in a separate fixture. If that requires changing the original frozen-loader/no-install constraint, name the exact change and obtain owner authorization; do not disguise it as ordinary Start or use another shell/transport.\n\nOwner choices for review:\n\n**A — recommended:** authorize only governed prevention/verified-normalization defects after reviewing this plan. Keep #2145 frozen; hold exact recovery and activation.\n\n**B:** additionally authorize a separate activation-contract design, with an explicit decision about which frozen-loader constraint may change. This would authorize design and qualification only; live installation or recovery still needs a concrete reviewed artifact and separate execution authorization.\n\nNeither choice is assumed. The follow-up spike's authorization does not select A or B.\n\n## Future execution sequence\n\n1. Owner reviews this plan and selects production scope. Create native defect issues with file ownership and the bounded stories above.\n2. Implement/review/test prevention and normalization independently. Run targeted integration tests, relevant existing suites, and repository-required verification against the exact candidate head. Broad suite success is not claimed by this spike.\n3. Qualify inspection/apply in a new physical fixture using production hooks/public CLI/ordinary writers; preserve every failure. Keep the full refusal matrix separate from artifact validation.\n4. Prove the reviewed activation operation is admitted by the actual old loader/host, or keep recovery held. No manual install, source edit or alternate transport may be substituted under the current constraints.\n5. Only after activation is proved and live recovery explicitly authorized, the original owner collects fresh original local/GitHub evidence and validates historical hashes. Mismatch means stop, not reset evidence to fit.\n6. Apply the reviewed digest-bound operation once, verify append-only history and ordinary binding/timer/generation readback, and report recovery independently of delivery, closure or #2071 proof.\n\n## Review focus and limits\n\nReview the absence of effects on refusals, attribution at fresh writes, treatment of partial remote effects, legacy provenance, full-history drift and selected-runtime activation separately. The spike prototypes exercise narrow behaviors only; the final production design must preserve broader existing preflight semantics. No full recovery implementation or activation contract has passed qualification. All production work awaits owner authorization.\n\n<!-- aitm-owned-comment key=\"spike.defect-plan-v2\" -->",

      "body": "# #2146 no-commit closure audit\n\nSTATUS: BLOCKED at Develop exit. The completed investigation is intact; the selected runtime has no registered deliverable-marker writer for a spike.       "body": "# #2146 archival validation design\n\nStatus: proposed for independent review; no candidate archive or verifier implemented.\n\n## Authority and purpose\n\nThe owning coordinator, acting under the human's explicit AFK authority, authorized an archival-validation increment for #2146 on 2026-11-05. It preserves and verifies the completed spike. It does not authorize another recovery experiment, a product policy change, native recovery of #2145, or changes to #2071, #2155 or #2159. Original source, raw evidence and refused fixtures remain untouched. The existing `2146-owner-deliverable-close` checkout will carry accepted changes; no new native chat or managed worktree is created.\n\nThe original verifier cannot run in native Test's Git-only sandbox because its ignored evidence is absent. A reviewed absolute-path alternative was rejected: the existing command grammar accepts it, but native receipt fingerprints do not bind external executable or evidence bytes and may reuse a receipt after those bytes drift. Preserve that finding, the failed native Test, the failed trunk CI setup, and subsequent successful e3 CI as historical records. None qualifies a new carrier commit.\n\n## Classification and lifecycle\n\nThis increment contains repository-only verification code, not merely documentation. Keep #2146's original spike identity and deliverable history; record the added executable scope explicitly. All genuine commits use `[#2146]` and receive a truthful commit trail. Do not attribute old source HEADs to this work.\n\nNo inspected contract requires a new issue: `deliver.mjs` takes the issue-resident no-commit route only when no PR exists; an actual PR takes the ordinary attributed code-delivery path. Therefore open a PR for this increment, run applicable code checks, targeted negative tests, complete exact-head CI, native Test and independent implementation review. Do not use the spike's testless defaults or a docs-only label to omit checks. Add explicit Functional DoD and VC coverage for the archival code through governed issue-body operations.\n\nRemain in Develop. Record the coordinator's explicit scope extension, exact accepted design/plan hashes and independent review through governed Scope/Plan Metadata and an owned continuation-authority audit. The original native Plan approval remains historical; do not describe this extension as a newly executed native Plan approval. `plan-approved-guard.mjs` applies at Plan exit only, and the story-quality contract does not retroactively reopen/demote Develop. Ordinary `plan-approve` requires Plan, `demote` does not support Develop-to-Plan, and later-stage exception repair does not apply here. Do not invoke those unsupported routes or manufacture a marker. A real subsequent gate refusal must be retained and resolved through its supported route.\n\n## Immutable inputs and measured format\n\nHistorical source commit: `2fd89e1103a0ee1976e0e1a1210c2d4e1bb57de0`.\nHistorical source tree: `36a4b5ba652094df909b05b4a99352bb7e41233d`.\nOriginal relative evidence root: `.scratch/native-recovery-spike/followup-20261103T233057Z`.\nOriginal absolute root: `/Users/kpburson/.codex/worktrees/3d20/ai-task-manager/.scratch/native-recovery-spike/followup-20261103T233057Z`.\n\nIndependent SHA-256 pins:\n\n- Manifest: `78afd54726726495057aacba467593b922b218d602081bf6b392274bc2514781`.\n- Original verifier: `e5a8f03a08a2e2b8d5dd9efc420e683d979d6a3b6911e64dd9bff260e8d6fc77`.\n- Original harness: `767fce262ef84ba7b1202519a9f95a4a10617a92ae74da37f9a27a481d0f82a1`.\n- Report: `c6c7c01006f77be50f24423f9280d47e07498c240a7dbd53eff9b2f29dc5cb8d`.\n- Plan: `1b20fedde2acd4a8e8c4bc41af74656e48932af101444fe21c674562f22b7dc1`.\n\nRead-only measurement rechecked every artifact digest: 1,133 manifest artifacts plus the manifest itself, 119,208,600 expanded bytes; 593 unique byte contents, 5,549,342 unique bytes. A sorted array of `[sha256, base64Bytes]` pairs plus a final newline is 7,442,466 bytes; gzip level 9 is 1,841,366 bytes; Brotli quality 11 is 590,016 bytes. Choose gzip for standard-tool inspectability; this is a format choice, not permission to publish unknown content. Candidate generation must reproduce the measurement or explain a format-only difference.\n\nCarrier data under `docs/archive/2146-native-recovery/`:\n\n- `index.json`: closed schema `aitm.spike-archive/v1`, original root/source/tree pins, archive digest/size, exact sorted list of 1,134 regular-file paths with SHA-256, size and permission bits, expected counts and total bytes. Independently pins original manifest and executable digests above.\n- `objects.json.gz`: deterministic gzip of the sorted unique-content array. No timestamps or host-dependent headers; no path entries or executable metadata inside this stream.\n- `README.md`: provenance, disclosure inventory, format inspection recipe, exact archive digest, original-versus-carrier claims and historical failures/review dispositions.\n\nNo original byte is edited, sanitized or omitted. All original artifact paths are reconstructed from the index; duplicates in content are deduplicated only in storage. The twelve source files are read from the exact historical Git commit, not copied from a mutable original worktree. Full historical Git object availability is a fail-closed precondition, never a network fallback.\n\n## Inventory and disclosure review\n\nThe approved scoped `rg` scans emitted only categories/counts/filenames. Selected GitHub/AWS/OpenAI/private-key/Google/Slack credential markers and password/access-token/refresh-token/GitHub-token labels had no matches. Known personal paths occur in 743 files and native identity markers in 415. All cookie-word hits are in 81 dependency inventories, which contain paths/modes/sizes/hashes rather than dependency contents. All twelve secret-word hits occur in nine qualification artifacts and match `/secret` and `secrets` fragments. Authorization words occur in report/plan/verifier boundaries. A broad `sk-` marker is noisy because it occurs within ordinary task-related words; a subsequent fixed-string whole-word `sk` scan had no matches, distinguishing a standalone conventional prefix from those embedded substrings. These are bounded pattern observations, not proof of universal credential absence. Retain the earlier Node scan refusal as a regex-as-path false positive; do not rewrite that failed attempt into success.\n\nBefore publication, compare the exact candidate inventory to the pinned original manifest, finish category triage without exposing credential values, and have the reviewer inspect the inventory and scan limits. Known native provenance IDs and local paths are retained faithfully under the explicit preservation authority. Any actual credential finding blocks publication; redaction would require a distinct derived artifact and could not satisfy this lossless design. Archive creation in ignored scratch is not publication.\n\n## Code and executable review boundary\n\nPlace all new runtime code under `scripts/research/2146-native-recovery/`, already excluded by package.json. Place tests under `scripts/tests/integration/task-tracker/core/2146-archive-validation.test.mjs` with `@story #2146`. Verify npm's actual pack inventory excludes archival code, tests and archive data. No package exports, command registry, hooks, policy or dependencies change.\n\nResponsibilities:\n\n- `archive.mjs`: deterministic pack/decode and strict read-set/path validation. Exposes pure bundle validation plus extraction into a newly created owned directory. No interpreter or provider execution.\n- `reconstruct.mjs`: obtains a disposable historical Git checkout using local immutable objects only; runs no old AITM CLI, provider seam, recovery action, or old hook. Owns only its new directory. Uses the carrier's required `scripts/task-tracker/lib/scratch-dir.mjs` helper; include this module and its transitive imports in implementation review. The historical I/O context remains built-ins-only.\n- `historical-context.mjs`: bounded file reads and historical absolute-output mapping; derives its root from its restored location. Uses Node built-ins only and independently checks the original manifest pin before reading its inventory. Does not import or execute the original harness.\n- `verify-historical.mjs`: reviewed derivative of the original verifier. Every original assertion remains; only its I/O imports, historical lookup mapping and truthful output-domain labels change. Retain an exact original-to-adapted diff in review evidence. No broad rewrite or formatter-only diff should conceal the changes.\n- `verify.mjs`: CLI `node scripts/research/2146-native-recovery/verify.mjs report|plan`. Requires clean current carrier source; checks carrier archive/index/executable bytes against their blobs at actual HEAD, validates the original independent pins, reconstructs, runs the adapted verifier, and reports both domains. No arbitrary root, archive, SHA or expected-hash CLI override.\n- `pack.mjs`: one-time local builder CLI taking the explicitly owned original evidence root and a new ignored output directory; refuses existing output and verifies all original pins before packaging. No publication or Git mutation.\n\nFor tests, internal library entrypoints may consume deliberately damaged bundles or reconstructed copies. They must not create a hidden CLI switch that weakens the production archive verification path. Positive native qualification uses the strict committed CLI only.\n\n## Historical reconstruction and subprocess contract\n\nAvoid checkout/restore commands that can invoke post-checkout hooks; `git restore` is not assumed hook-free. The reconstruction implementation must be reviewed against the local Git version before its first candidate run.\n\nProposed minimal isolation is a NEW disposable physical Git repository under the approved repository-local isolated test-fixture root returned by `mkdtempProjectIsolated('2146-archive-')`, not a native worktree or AITM binding. Use local `git clone --shared --no-checkout --template=<new-empty-template> -- <real-current-carrier-root> <new-reconstruction-root>`; the empty template applies only to creation of this validation repository, never modifies or disables an existing hook or native guard. Refuse any applicable global/system Git hook configuration before creation and any active hook/filter configuration in the new repository before index/worktree mutation. If this cannot be established without an override, stop this reconstruction path rather than silently disabling a guard.\n\nUse a small checked runner for this fixed Git command set only. Before any child Git invocation, reject nonempty inherited `GIT_*` variables except the harmless exact values `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0` and `GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0`; in particular do not strip or override redirected repository, index, object, config, template, helper or trace destinations. Before clone, inspect applicable global/system configuration with includes for hooks, filters, filesystem monitoring, transport helpers and URL rewrites; before update-ref/read-tree/status inspect the new repository's effective configuration as well. Refuse executable `core.fsmonitor`, active hooks/filters, `url.*.insteadOf`/`pushInsteadOf`, proxy/SSH helper commands and other settings that would execute a helper for these operations. A false/disabled filesystem-monitor setting is harmless; do not disable an active one. Only a physically validated local carrier directory is a permitted clone source; no arbitrary URL/ref/root CLI input. This is not a general Git sandbox framework, and no global configuration is changed. Candidate tests must include inherited `GIT_INDEX_FILE`, `GIT_DIR`, `GIT_CONFIG_COUNT`, fsmonitor/helper configuration and URL rewriting, and verify refusal occurs before external writes/helper execution.\n\nSet only the new repository's detached HEAD to the exact historical commit using `git update-ref --no-deref HEAD <pin>` and populate only its new index/worktree with `git read-tree --reset -u <pin>`. This is not a reset or ref change in the carrier/original repository. Validate the historical commit/tree, clean status and all twelve source hashes. The read-only local object-store dependency may point to the carrier Git objects, never original raw evidence or live runtime. No network Git, provider command, old hook, old CLI, identity variable override or copied runtime is allowed. Record exact subprocess argv and outcome categories for review; do not print raw credential material.\n\nThe shared clone does not register another worktree in the owning repository. Remove only the exact newly created owned directory on success. Preserve unexpected local candidate failures and their diagnostics. Native Test/CI retain their normal sandbox lifecycle; do not claim those runners preserve removed filesystem fixtures.\n\n## Extraction and read containment\n\nDecode only the closed schema and fixed counts. Require canonical sorted arrays, unique path names and unique object hashes; reject extra keys, repeated normalized names, unexpected/missing members, unknown object references, noncanonical base64, incorrect size/hash, oversized compressed/decompressed/expanded data, and wrong pins. Gzip inflation is bounded to 8 MiB, compressed input to 2 MiB and expanded logical files to 120 MiB. Every original pin and original inventory entry must match, not merely the self-reported outer index.\n\nOnly regular files are representable. Reject symlinks, hardlink declarations, non-regular source files, absolute paths, backslashes, empty/dot/dot-dot segments, NULs, `.git` segments and path-prefix collisions. Check each existing destination ancestor with lstat; require the empty destination's real path to remain within its newly owned root; use exclusive file creation and never overwrite. Create the private owned root with owner-only permissions and do not share its path with another writer. The concurrency assumption is no hostile same-user process replacing ancestors between checks and writes: a tested pre-write symlink replacement must refuse, but pathname lstat/create checks are not claimed to be race-proof against arbitrary same-user interference. Review the actual write sequence. No tar extraction, pathname globbing, shell, external decompressor or archive-specified permission outside ordinary file modes.\n\nHistorical `r.out` mapping requires the exact original evidence root followed by `/`, then a canonical relative RUN DIRECTORY belonging to the ancestor-directory set derived from the validated file inventory. `r.out` itself is not an inventory file. Every subsequent file read must match an exact permitted file in the inventory. Include a positive recorded run-directory shape and negatives for an unrelated directory, old-root prefix collision, traversal and foreign absolute root. Never fall back to the original filesystem. Keep recorded JSON bytes unchanged. The bounded I/O context permits reads only of original inventory files, original manifest and twelve historical source paths, with physical ancestor checks. Extra validation modules are pinned and copied separately; they are not relabeled as original artifacts.\n\n## Assertions and claims\n\nKeep all original source-HEAD/clean-tree/source-hash assertions in the reconstructed historical checkout, all 1,133 artifact hashes, matrix and evidence references, per-run executable identities/dependency outcomes, baseline/runtime preservation, actor and timing invariants, partial-write/readback outcomes, unexpected reflog acceptance, blocked activation, transport qualification, failed prevention assertions, rejected remote-Git ledger cases and truthful report/plan language. No missing or expected-refusal result becomes a pass.\n\nThe result separately names `archiveCarrierCommit`, `archiveCarrierClean`, `historicalSourceCommit`, `historicalSourceTree`, `historicalReconstructionClean`, archive/manifest/adapter digests, 81 execution records and 16 matrix cases. Keep `exactRecovery: UNIMPLEMENTED` and `nativeHostActivation: UNPROVEN`. Never emit undifferentiated `sourceClean: true` or claim reconstruction proves the original live checkout is currently clean. Native receipts remain at the actual carrier HEAD. Tracked archive and executable bytes are therefore part of immutable commit authority and drift invalidates ordinary receipt freshness.\n\n## Required qualification\n\nNegative cases must exercise the actual archive validator and actual adapted verifier: altered archive byte, replaced original manifest, missing/extra file, wrong source commit/tree/source bytes, executable identity drift, runtime/baseline invariant drift, absolute/traversal/duplicate paths, original-prefix collision, symlink/hardlink escape, oversized inflation, unsupported mode and missing historical Git object. To reach deep original assertions in a disposable negative fixture, update only that fixture's self-consistency manifest and run the actual adapted assertion module; separately prove the strict outer CLI refuses any such changed original manifest. Never modify original evidence or weaken the normal CLI pins.\n\nQualify both modes from a clean Git-only checkout on the intended carrier source, without access to the original evidence root; verify no old CLI/hooks/provider execution, no original/carrier ref/index change, no external writes and no shipped archive/tooling. Current CI fast/integration shards declare `fetch-depth: 0`; slow shards do not. Put these checks in the integration lane and make the actual CI test assert `cat-file` availability of the exact historical commit/tree and execute both modes. Static workflow inspection and local ancestry are supporting evidence only. The actual native Test sandbox must perform the same object-availability check and complete verification; a missing object is a failure, never a fetch or skip. Run full lint/format, targeted negative tests and complete exact-head CI. Native Test must then run the new VCs with fresh develop finalization and a coordinator-reserved Test slot. Review and delivery/close follow normal exact-head gates; old e3 CI or original AC stamps cannot be relabeled as new execution.\n\n<!-- aitm-owned-comment key=\"spike.archival-design-v1\" -->",

      "body": "# #2146 Archival Validation Implementation Plan\n\n> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. > Mirrored from comment #issuecomment-6610204792 (https://github.com/kburson/ai-task-manager/issues/2146#issuecomment-6610204792). Comment is the diff-history canonical; this body copy is the gate-canonical source.

### Story Intent

- **Beneficiary:** native-session operator
- **Capability:** assess an attributable recovery route for the preserved partial initial-branch attempt
- **Need:** partial branch creation has left the original session unable to continue
- **Value or failure prevented:** choose a reviewed correction without losing the original timer, ownership or recovery evidence

### Scope and authorization

This is #2146, an independent spike originating in #2145. The owner authorized investigation and disposable experiments at 2026-11-03T15:59:49.908Z and subsequently authorized resolving its issue-creation blocker through supported AITM workflows. Production implementation remains unauthorized. Deliver a feasibility report and a proposed defect implementation plan; do not recover or mutate #2145, execute the #2071 bridge proof, or modify old worktrees. Positive and negative findings must remain distinct from source-only hypotheses.

### Current evidence and source map

The checkout is pinned to 2fd89e1103a0ee1976e0e1a1210c2d4e1bb57de0. The registered public create-issue operation succeeded after direct helper invocation was hook-refused. Native Start created the #2146 actor/binding/timer normally. Missing last-known-state was normalized with native reconcile while detached and verified by GitHub readback. Empty User Story was accepted at intake but caused Explain scope collection to fail; the governed user-story operation repaired it and fresh Explain became ready. Direct bin/aitm.mjs draft-branch then completed with the same generation and timer start. These observations demonstrate a prevention sequence in this new checkout, not recovery of #2145.

scripts/task-tracker/draft-branch.mjs reads live board/ownership and location, then creates an undated journal and switches branches before ordinary Start renewal. It does not check the last-known-state marker before those effects. lib/native-branch-renewal.mjs enforces exact native carrier, original generation, clean physical source/index/ref/reflog, singleton owner, body/board state equality, and latest durable location equality. The final state and location checks explain why the supplied partial attempt cannot pass current renewal even after state normalization alone.

task-tracker.mjs calls enforceIssueWorktreeLocation before runVerbPreflight. lib/worktree-relocation-guard.mjs obtains the session with fallback-to-empty behavior, writes location through mutateIssueBody, and excludes reconcile from the guarded verb set. lib/issue-worktree-location.mjs validates structural history but location equality ignores SID. state.mjs loads actor timing, and lib/timing-actor.mjs rejects default-session. Together these source paths match the supplied terminal sequence: an unattributed named location can be appended before timing refuses. This is not yet a reproduced result in a disposable fixture.

verbs/reconcile.mjs accept-live stamps another visit, ignores the returned writeIssueBodyWithRetry outcome, then persists local state. Its stdout is insufficient evidence. #2146 used actual body/board readback; its second Backlog entry remains history.

Existing integration/native-branch-observation tests exercise physical Git but call the inspector directly with substituted remote reads. Existing disposable-worktree-lifecycle tests replace renewBinding with setActiveTask. Neither establishes public-hook/public-CLI recovery of the preserved failure. The spike must not cite those seams as proof of ordinary renewal.

### Investigation plan and timebox

Bound this investigation to 90 minutes of native tracked work starting at the successful #2146 bind (2026-11-03T16:46:18.869Z); stop new experiments by 18:01 UTC to reserve 15 minutes for report, plan and checkpoint, with a hard review handoff at 18:16 UTC. Native timing may report Unknown; do not fabricate precise active minutes from wall time. This clock is independent of all #2071 estimates and the later bridge-proof clock. The proposed breakdown is admission/refinement/planning 20 minutes, disposable baseline reproduction 25 minutes, bounded candidate/refusal and activation investigation 25 minutes, findings/defect plan/review 20 minutes. Actual admission overhead reduces experiment coverage rather than extending scope automatically.

First reproduce missing-state draft renewal and no-native-session Start location mutation in physical disposable Git repositories. Use the pinned production hook/public CLI and ordinary state/location/binding writers. Keep inherited genuine native identity for the positive fixture; isolate all provider data under .scratch and intercept only provider transport. The test harness must refuse any unhandled provider request and any remote Git write. Do not copy live runtime. Preserve fixture roots and all unsuccessful logs. If the necessary harness cannot satisfy these boundaries, report that blocker instead of using a weaker proof.

Only after both baseline reproductions, experiment with one small throwaway candidate at a time. Candidate A checks actor and applicable semantic authority before location mutation and again under the issue lock. Candidate B admits only a digest-bound initial-branch recovery manifest that binds original generation/timer, physical ref/reflog, journal and both exact historical locations, preserving them with an append-only correction. Candidate C validates missing state before journal/checkout and reads normalization back. The final report will state which candidate classes were actually exercised.

Required matrix: missing/wrong actor; malformed or conflicting state; journal mismatch; owner/generation/timer drift; dirty tracked, staged, untracked, source/ref/reflog drift; remote owner/state/location drift at lock/write; provider write and readback failure; history preservation; no-push. For every required case record pass, refusal, not run or blocked, with its scope and commands. Do not turn a not-run case into a pass.

Activation is an independent feasibility condition. Trace the installed/scoped-versus-repo-relative hook and public-entry selection. Establish whether reviewed support can become the actually selected runtime of the preserved blocked checkout without source-byte drift, manual installation, copied state, live merge/rebase/push or an alternate command evading the old hook. If no route qualifies, classify recovery as blocked even if a throwaway candidate algorithm passes.

### Deliverables and verification

Keep throwaway scripts, fixtures and logs under .scratch/native-recovery-spike. Publish findings and the proposed defect plan through #2146's governed comment/artifact operations. The report verifier must check artifact inventory, source identities and explicit matrix coverage without treating missing runs as passing. The plan verifier must require owned files/interfaces, failing-first cases, activation/recovery sequence, preserved-history requirements and the production-authorization boundary. No source commits are intended; never attribute the pinned HEAD to #2146 as a commit trail.

### Risks and limits

No #2145 local runtime has been read by this chat; exact local historical facts come from its owning handoff. GitHub #2145 was read-only checked and still contains both supplied locations. Reproduction in disposable repositories can establish algorithm behavior, not prove the live preserved attempt remains unchanged. Any future recovery must obtain fresh exact-attempt evidence from its owner. Fixture transport must be documented separately from runtime activation. A reviewed implementation plan is a proposal, not implementation or approval.
